answer.generated: When an entity E is described as a generalization of entities E1, ..., En, it means that E represents a more abstract or overarching concept that includes all the specific instances of E1 through En. This establishes a hierarchical structure where E acts as the parent entity, while E1, ..., En are its child entities, each representing a particular case or specialization of E. The generalization relationship thus defines a subset relation: every instance of E1, ..., En is also an instance of E, but not vice versa. This allows modeling complex real-world concepts by capturing commonalities and variations through a single entity and its specializations.
